summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored Hong Kong CIES / New CIES documents (ImmD statistics pages and Review annexes, InvestHK press releases and results slides, government press releases, LegCo replies). Most programme numbers were already in the dataset; this pass adds New CIES enquiries, investment percentages by asset class, the first-year application count from the 2026 appendix, the 2025 extension-of-stay application, a 440% monthly rise, CIES Investment Portfolio allocations, the 11% invested-before-applying share from the 2010 release, rule rows from four releases and two events.

program_terms.applies_to: aggregate net asset value managed by the applicant's family's eligible single family office (condition for holding the investment through a private company)
program_terms.quote: managed by an Eligible Single Family Office of the Applicant/Entrant’s family as defined in section 2 of Schedule 16E to the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112 of the Laws of Hong Kong), which manages assets specified under Schedule 16C to the Inland Revenue Ordinance for the FIHV(s) of the family with an aggregate Net asset value of not less than HK$240 million.
program_terms.notes: Not an investment threshold: a condition for counting investments held through a wholly owned Hong Kong private company in the form of a Family-owned Investment Holding Vehicle (FIHV) or its special purpose entity. The FIHV must also have at least two full-time employees in Hong Kong and HK$2 million annual operating expenditure there (next row). Effective 1 March 2026 per the page title.

program_terms.applies_to: annual operating expenditure in Hong Kong of the Family-owned Investment Holding Vehicle (condition for holding the investment through a private company)
program_terms.location: bullet 4 of the conditions and footnote *
program_terms.quote: where the FIHV has at least two full-time employees in Hong Kong and incurs at least HK$2 million operating expenditure annually in Hong Kong to carry out the activities of FIHV*
program_terms.notes: Condition on the holding vehicle, not an investment. Footnote: an FIHV set up less than one year earlier must incur the amount by the end of its first year and each later year. Effective 1 March 2026 per the page title.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant (with spouse and unmarried dependent children under 18)
program_terms.quote: An eligible applicant must make investment of a minimum of HK$30 million in the permissible investment assets.
program_terms.notes: Same threshold as the FSTB LegCo brief row; this release gives no split into HK$27m and HK$3m. Permission to stay normally two years, then three-year extensions; permanent residence after seven years' continuous ordinary residence.

program_terms.quote: According to the existing Rules for CIES, applications will be accepted if they involve the investment of no less than HK$10 million in permissible investment assets and such applications are made within six months of the investment.
program_terms.notes: The rule in force up to suspension; this release does not give its start date (14 Oct 2010 per hkg-isd-pr-cies-amended-2010). Transitional arrangement: applications made after 15 Jan 2015 still accepted for HK$10m investments made in the six months before the suspension date, if the application is made within six months of the investment.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant aged 18 or above (with spouse and unmarried dependent children under 18)
program_terms.quote: An applicant must make an investment of a minimum of HK$30 million in the permissible investment assets, including investing a minimum of HK$27 million in the permissible financial assets and non-residential real estate (at Annex), and placing HK$3 million into a new CIES Investment Portfolio.
program_terms.notes: The release gives no start date (the scheme was to open in mid-2024); valid_from follows the launch date (1 Mar 2024, hkg-investhk-pr-new-cies-opens-2024), as for the FSTB LegCo brief rows.

program_terms.quote: including investing a minimum of HK$27 million in the permissible financial assets and non-residential real estate (at Annex)
program_terms.notes: The release gives no start date (the scheme was to open in mid-2024); valid_from follows the launch date (1 Mar 2024, hkg-investhk-pr-new-cies-opens-2024), as for the FSTB LegCo brief rows. The annex listing the permissible assets is a separate attachment, not stored.

program_terms.quote: and placing HK$3 million into a new CIES Investment Portfolio.
program_terms.notes: The release gives no start date (the scheme was to open in mid-2024); valid_from follows the launch date (1 Mar 2024, hkg-investhk-pr-new-cies-opens-2024), as for the FSTB LegCo brief rows. Managed by the Hong Kong Investment Corporation Limited.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's net assets, held throughout the two years before applying
program_terms.quote: An applicant must demonstrate that he/she has net assets of not less than HK$30 million to which he/she is absolutely beneficially entitled throughout the two years preceding the application.
program_terms.notes: Eligibility condition, not an investment. The release gives no start date (the scheme was to open in mid-2024); valid_from follows the launch date (1 Mar 2024, hkg-investhk-pr-new-cies-opens-2024), as for the FSTB LegCo brief rows. valid_to is the day before the six-month rule took effect (hkg-fstb-pr-new-cies-enhancements-2025).

events.title: Holding-company conditions published (family-office vehicle)
events.description: InvestHK's page on the 1 March 2026 measure: an applicant may hold the investment in a wholly owned Hong Kong private company used only for permissible assets, in the form of a Family-owned Investment Holding Vehicle (at least two full-time staff and HK$2m yearly spending in Hong Kong) managed by the family's eligible single family office with at least HK$240m in assets; holdings may be transferred to it during the stay to use the family-office tax concessions. Same measure as the event sourced from hkg-investhk-pr-new-cies-two-year-2026.
events.quote: Below is the summary of the new measure on the New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme effective from 1 March 2026.

events.title: Online applications opened; paper forms until 15 October 2024
events.description: Applicants can submit the Net Asset Assessment and Assessment on Investment Requirements forms online; paper forms accepted on or before 15 October 2024. A Certified Public Accountant (Practising) must be engaged, at the applicant's cost, to issue the fulfilment documents before submitting.
events.quote: Invest Hong Kong (InvestHK) announced today (September 16) that the applicants of the New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (the New CIES) can now submit application forms for Net Asset Assessment and Assessment on Investment Requirements online.

new_indicators.name: Share of programme investment by asset class or route
new_indicators.definition: Percentage of the total qualifying investment made (or verified) under a residence- or citizenship-by-investment programme that went into one asset class or route, in a period, as printed by the source. Never calculated by us. Use breakdown route=. Companion to rbi_investment_total.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-hkg2 for the InvestHK New CIES distribution tables (25 May 2025 and 2 March 2026), which print amounts and percentages side by side.

new_indicators.name: Change in applications received (percent, as stated)
new_indicators.definition: Percentage change in a programme's applications between a period and an earlier period, as stated by the source when it gives no counts. Never calculated by us. Notes say the comparison period and what is counted.
new_indicators.notes: Same proposal as extract-cbi-kna1 (repeated here in case that batch is merged later); used for the New CIES March 2025 rise of over 440% on February.

Amounts add up: 6,008+4,632+2,155+1,434+627+1,629 = 16,485; percentages add to 100.0; column A + column B = total for every count row.

InvestHK press release of 16 Sept 2024: online application platform launched, paper forms accepted until 15 Oct 2024, CPA (Practising) fulfilment documents required; key numbers as of 13 Sept 2024 (enquiries over 5 000, applications over 500, net-asset verifications 448, investment verifications 47, expected investment over HK$15 billion). Four numbers were already recorded; this pass adds enquiries and the online-platform event.

InvestHK press release of 1 March 2024: the New CIES opens for applications; HK$30 million minimum investment; dependants; two-year stay then three-year extensions; permanent residence after seven years; roles of InvestHK and ImmD; quotes. No statistics. The launch event was already recorded; this pass adds the HK$30m rule row from this source.

InvestHK press release of 16 Oct 2024: from 16 Oct 2024 residential property counts if a single property costs HK$50 million or more; all real estate together counts for at most HK$10 million; rules updated; details of the 1 March 2025 private-company measure to follow. The HK$50m rule row and the event were already recorded (the HK$10m cap is in that rule row's notes). Nothing added.

InvestHK press release of 2 March 2026 (two-year milestone): applications 3 166, formal approvals 1 762, expected investment about HK$95 billion (as at 28 Feb 2026); investment amount and percentage by asset class; 1 March 2026 private holding company change; CIES Investment Portfolio 2025 batch allocations exceeding HK$3 billion; quotes and promotion. The headline 'nearly 3 200' rounds the printed 3 166 and is not added. Already recorded: 10 numbers and the event. Added: percentage shares (6; printed Total 100.0% not added) and the HK$3 billion portfolio allocations. Amounts add up to 55,636; percentages to 100.0.

Two-page appendix to the 2 March 2026 press release: Chart 1, applications received by scheme year (918 Mar 2024-Feb 2025; 2 248 Mar 2025-Feb 2026; +145%); Chart 2, investment amount and percentage by asset class as of 28 Feb 2026 (table plus a pie chart, read by OCR, repeating the percentages). Already recorded: 2 248. Added: 918, the six amounts and total, and the six percentages (printed Total 100.0% not added). The 145% is not added because both counts are printed. Parts add up to 55,636 and 100.0%.

InvestHK 2026 1H results highlights (5 slides): InvestHK's completed projects (413), direct investment (HK$53+ billion), jobs (8,600+), projects by place of origin and sector (out of scope: general inward investment, not the programme); slide 4, New CIES 1 Mar 2024-18 Jun 2026: 3,967 applications, 2,377 formal approvals, expected investment HK$119+ billion (in HKD), all already recorded and re-checked (slide also OCR-checked); slide 5, strategy text. Nothing added.

Government press release of 30 Sept 2003: the CIES will accept applications from 27 Oct 2003; HK$6.5 million minimum in real estate and/or specified financial assets; eligible groups (not Mainland residents); six-month investment windows; portfolio maintenance (no top-up if value falls); dependants; right of abode after seven years. No statistics. The rule row and the launch event were already recorded. Nothing added.

Government press release of 13 Oct 2010: from 14 Oct 2010 threshold raised from HK$6.5m to HK$10m and real estate suspended; insurers allowed as intermediaries; threshold to be reviewed every three years; transitional arrangement; around 11% of entrants invested before applying; since 2003 around 8,200 investors and 15,500 dependants admitted, around $58 billion invested (printed with a bare '$'; the existing row records HKD, following the dataset's practice for Hong Kong Government releases, which is a pending decision). The three cumulative figures, the rule row and the event were already recorded. Added: the 11% share. The insurer change is already an event from hkg-immd-cies-announcement-2012.

Government press release of 14 Jan 2015: CIES suspended from 15 Jan 2015 until further notice, with reasons; over 12 000 applications under processing; pending and approved applications unaffected; HK$10 million rule and transitional arrangement. The 12 000 pending figure and the closure event were already recorded. Added: the HK$10m rule row from this source.

Government press release of 19 Dec 2023: details of the New CIES (eligible groups aged 18+, HK$30m net assets over two years, HK$30m investment: HK$27m in financial assets and non-residential real estate plus HK$3m in the CIES Investment Portfolio; dependants; stay periods; permanent residence after seven years or unconditional stay; planned stamp-duty suspension for residential purchases; InvestHK/ImmD roles; launch planned for mid-2024). No statistics. The approval event is already recorded from the FSTB brief. Added: four rule rows from this source. The annex listing permissible assets is a separate attachment not in the stored file.

LegCo written reply of 27 April 2005: no specific performance target; ImmD uses the pledge for other entry visas (90% finalised within six weeks of complete documents) and has met it; staffing (four Immigration Officer grade staff and one civilian); since launch 764 applications received, 145 still being processed, 371 formal approvals, 122 approvals-in-principle; publicity. The four application counts were already recorded and re-checked (the reply does not say how the remaining completed cases ended, so no total check is possible). Nothing added.
